contexts.text: With difficulty, if ever, can they be brought to receive truths.
What flows in, is received according to the state. AC 1980:end. AC 2284:2.
Diversely according to the reception of life.
Conjugial love is diversely received; and, as it is received, such does it become...

Affection is the receiving [agent] itself. To receive anything against the affection, is to receive it against the life; therefore, the truth of doctrine cannot be received except by the affection of it; and, such as is the affection, such is the reception...
Life is received by everyone according to his nature.
The reception of faith. Treated of. AC 2913.
A new Church which was kindly received.
With those not in goods... there is no plane, nor soil, thus no recipient.
Hear us = reception.
The Lord's joy on account of a kind reception. Signified, Explained.
Those with whom the truth and good of faith can be received. Signified. AC 2940. AC 2951. AC 2963.
Reception is first, being of the understanding.
A state of reception. Signified. AC 2958.
The price of redemption is predicated of the reception by man, with whom it is great according to the reception.
Why one receives differently from another.
Without the good of life there is no reception; and, where there is no reception, there is no trust.
To this life the recipients correspond... The recipients, according to what they are, so they live...
For all Salvation is... by the reception of the Divine good.

Truth... is not received by good, unless there is consent... Consent is acknowledgement itself; through this is reception effected... and when truth... has been received by the will... the man is regenerate.
For the giver and the recipient are as agent and patient.
For the good in man is what receives the Word.
The Divine love is received variously...
Truth... is given according to their apprehension; for thus it is received... otherwise, there would be no reception, because no acknowledgement.
Good in aspect = what is easily received.
A state of reception. Signified.
The reception of truth by the spiritual is here treated of.
Spiritual truth received because it is called Divine...
To kill, when predicated of good and truth, = not to be received.
It is charity which receives faith.
Hand = power, thus the faculty of receiving.
For good receives no other.
Celestial good and spiritual truth... impart the power to receive each of them...
The influx is the same... but it is received differently.
Angels, Spirits, and men, are only recipients of life.
Still, the evil, and the infernals also, are forms recipient of life...
For man receives only so much from others, as he either has of his own, or acquires by looking into the matter in himself.
To conceive = reception. AC 3955.

The esse of man is nothing else than a recipient of the eternal which proceeds from the Lord; for men, Spirits, and Angels are nothing but recipients, or forms recipient, of life from the Lord. The reception of life is that of which existere is predicated.
If there is not in men... something recipient of good and truth, as a ground, or plane, the inflowing good and truth cannot be received.
The faculty of receiving and acknowledging. Signified.
The reception of truth. Treated of.

This light... affects all according to the reception. Those in evil do not receive the Divine good... But the Divine truth can be received even by the evil, but only by their external man... So, when the heat of the sun is received... But when the light alone is received, nothing vegetates...
(Those who) receive Divine truth in good (are signified by) as many as received ().
For the Divine good cannot be received even by an Angel... but the Divine truth can be received... in which Divine good can dwell, with a difference according to the reception.
The Lord is present with everyone, but according to the reception. Explained.
Not because there are various things in the Lord, but because His Divine is variously received by men. Explained.
Those who in the life of the body had received Divine things...
To dispose... to receive the good represented by Esau. Signified. AC 4252. a.[end].
According to the reception of good by truths.
The light is according to the reception.
The Rational receives truths and goods before and more easily than the Natural.

Unless there were reception of it in the Second Heaven, the wisdom (in the Third Heaven) would be dissipated: and so unless there were a reception of the light and intelligence of the Second Heaven in the First; and, finally, of that of the First Heaven in the Natural of man, the intelligence of these Heavens would be dissipated, unless it was provided... that there should be reception elsewhere; and therefore the Heavens have been formed so that the one may serve the other for reception; and, at last, that man, as to his Natural and Sensuous, may serve for ultimate reception...
They went forth to meet the Bridegroom = their reception.
Believing that Heaven is only reception.
The light of Heaven is varied with everyone according to the reception.
If they have confirmed themselves against Divine truths in both doctrine and life, they... can never be brought to receive them...
The gentiles... easily receive Divine truths...
No one can ever receive the truths of faith unless he is in the life of charity.
Those in love towards the neighbour can receive all the truths of faith... But those in the love of self can never receive them... except for the sake of their own honour and gain...
Such as the loves are, such are the lives, because such are the receptions of life: love towards the neighbour receives the life of Heaven; and the love of self receives the life of Hell.

Hence those only who have lived in charity are received into Heaven; and, from charity, they are in the potency to receive and imbue all truths. But with those in separated faith... their loves receive such things as are in agreement with them...

There are evil Spirits who... receive the truths of faith... and even receive them with desire; but not... to live according to them; but to glory over others... For man's Intellectual is such that it can receive truths; but still the truths are not appropriated to them unless they live according to them.
Conception = the reception of the truth of faith... and reception is effected when the truth of the understanding passes into the good of the will...
In pangs to bring forth = received with difficulty.
When in humiliation, he is in a state of the reception of good and truth.
If reception into Heaven were of mercy alone, all would be received into Heaven.

As the good have received Divine truth, they are judged from good... and as the evil have not received Divine truth, they are judged from truth... To receive Divine truth is not only to have faith, but also to act faith...
As man has reciprocality, he has reception, which is impossible with beasts.
The Lord is always rising (as a Sun) with everyone who receives the truth which is of faith and the good which is of love, but is setting with everyone who does not receive them. Explained.

As the inmost of man is such that he can receive the Divine, and not only receive it, but also appropriate it to himself by acknowledgement and affection, thus by reciprocality... he can never die; for he is in what is eternal and infinite, not only by influx thence, but also by reception.
The influx of the interior Natural into the exterior, and the beginning of reception. Signified, Explained.
But the things which inflow, are changed according to the reception...
The reception of faith. Signified, Explained.
Without administering means... the end... cannot be received. Therefore, man's interior and exterior things... must be reduced to correspondence, in order that he may receive the Divine influx.
In every degree (the influent good) is qualified according to the reception. AC 5144:5.
The inmost is in the most perfect state, and therefore it can receive good from the Lord immediately...

As to the influx of celestial good... and its reception, it is to be known that the Voluntary receives good, and the Intellectual receives truth; and that the Intellectual cannot receive truth so as to appropriate it, unless the Voluntary receives good at the same time; and contrariwise; for the one inflows into the other, and disposes it to receive.
Good the influent; truth the recipient.

The Lord continually inflows with good... and man either receives it or does not receive it. If he receives, it is well with him; but if he does not receive, it is evil with him. If, when he does not receive, he feels anything of anxiety... there is hope that he can be reformed...
Ye would not hearken = no reception.
There must be delight in order that man may receive...

Truth in powers denotes in the faculties of receiving... but the faculties or powers of receiving truth are entirely according to good... In the other life, those in good have the faculty of not only perceiving truth, but also of receiving it, according to the quality and quantity of the good in which they are. But those in evil have no faculty of receiving truth. Explained... Moreover, every man of sound mind is in the faculty of receiving truths; but those who turn themselves to evil extinguish this faculty, whereas those who turn themselves to good elevate it.
Life is one... but it is variously received... AC 6467.
For, when man is in humiliation, he can receive good from the Lord. Explained.

In the first time of the Church, truth is received, because they are in good... In the last time, nothing of truth is received, because they are not in good; for, when man is not in... charity towards the neighbour, if the greatest truths are told him, he does not receive them. Explained.
In proportion to the good in the external man, in the same proportion the good which inflows from the Lord is received there.
That the Internal from the Natural procured the faculties of receiving good. Signified, Explained.
For faculty is receptibility. Explained.
Unless the good of love inflowed from the Lord, no man would possess the faculty of receiving either truth or good. (This) influx causes all things within man to be disposed for reception.

The faculties of receiving truth and good with man are immediately from the Lord... for man is always kept in the faculty of receiving good and truth: from this faculty he has understanding and will; and the reason he does not receive, is that he then turns himself to evil... AC 6148:11. Signified.
That man contributes nothing to the faculty of receiving good and truth, is known...
The things of the literal sense are general vessels which receive truths...
(When confirmed by the letter) if they were to hear the truth itself from Heaven, they would not receive it.
As they have not closed the interiors, they are in the faculty of receiving goods and truths.
Unless (after death) a man has been in spiritual good through faith, there is not anything which receives the good which inflows from the Lord...
That from His Divine Human would proceed the truths which could be received. Signified, Explained.
Thus the Divine Spiritual and the Divine Celestial are so called relatively to the receptions.
(The Divine truth and the Divine good) are variously received by man, namely, according to his quality. The Lord does not compel man to receive that which inflows from Himself...
That it may be well received. Signified.
Reception from love. Signified.
Everyone receives truth in proportion as he is in good.
For nothing receives truth but good.
They would not receive unless they saw... signs. Explained.
The reception of Divine truth. Signified.
The reception of the Divine influx. Signified, Explained.
The truth which proceeds from the Lord immediately... cannot be received by any living finite substance...
For (the evil) have not received the Divine good... But the good... have received it.
That those in falsities will not receive. Signified.
For the ground which receives is the illustrated Rational.

Even evil men have Angels with them, in order that they may be able... to receive influx from Heaven... But when, from their life here, they are such that they cannot receive the influx of truth and good from Heaven, the Angels and good Spirits recede from them.
That those in evils from falsities did not receive. Signified.
Only truths receive the light which illustrates.
In proportion as man receives the affection of love towards the neighbour, in the same proportion he receives the truths of faith. Hence it is that the infernals... cannot receive them.

When man is in this essential (humiliation), he is then in a state of receiving from the Lord the truth of faith and the good of charity... But if man exalts himself before the Lord, he then closes the interiors of his mind for the reception of good and truth from the Lord.
To collect = to receive.
For the good which inflows from the Lord is not given in proportion to their desire; but in proportion as they can receive it.
A state of reception and application to (the good signified by the manna, and the delight signified by the quails). Signified, Explained.

To approach = influx, and therefore also reception; for reception is the reciprocal of influx; for they correspond to each other... and reception is not anything, unless there is also application, namely, to use...
Reception and appropriation according to the faculty of each person. Signified.
Reception according to the power of each Society. Signified, Explained.
Everyone there is in the power of receiving, according to the quality and quantity of the good acquired in the world.
For men and Angels are only recipients, or forms accommodated to receive life, thus good and truth, from the Lord.
The reception of truth before it is conjoined with good. Signified, Explained.
To drink = to be instructed in the truths of faith, and to receive them.
For it is the reception of the Lord's mercy... by which everyone is saved. Those who receive it in the world, in the other life are in it; for they are then in the faculty of receiving it.

In proportion as man receives from the truths of faith, in the same proportion he enters into the light of intelligence, and is elevated into Heaven. But the reception of the truths of faith is not effected by mere acknowledgement, but by acknowledgement conjoined with life...
treats of the preparation to receive the truth Divine from the Lord out of Heaven.
The reception of truth. Signified.
The reception (of what was from the Divine). Signified.
Truth Divine is not received by anyone, unless it is accommodated to the apprehension...
Truth Divine through the Heavens... perfects the good, because these receive the Divine good which is in the truth; but it destroys the evil, because they do not receive the Divine good in it.
A holy tremor with those who would receive. Signified, Explained.
But reception is according to the good with everyone...
The power of truth from the Divine to prepare them to receive the Divine. Signified.
And keep My commandments = who receive the truths of faith. Explained.
For evils and falsities must be removed before the truth and good which are from the Lord can be received.
The reception of truth in an accommodated form. Signified, Explained.
By which they are in a state to receive the truths of faith and the goods of charity from the Lord.
No reception of truth. Signified, Explained.
The reception of good from mercy. Signified, Explained.
Instruction concerning the precepts of faith, and reception. Signified, Explained.
To hear = to receive in the memory and be instructed; to receive in the understanding and believe; and to receive in obedience and do. Illustrated.
No others are regenerated than those who receive the Lord's mercy in faith and life here; according to, As many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God... ().
To receive and take into possession the interior truths of faith; and to receive and take into possession the interior goods of faith. Signified.
Reception in the understanding by those who are truly of the Church. Signified, Explained.
Reception then in the heart. Signified.
The Divine truth received by man. Representation and Explained.
The reception of the truth proceeding from the Divine Human. Signified, Explained.
Adaptation to receive by man. Signified, Explained.
The Lord continually inflows with the good of love and the truths of faith, but these are dissimilarly received...
The reception [by the Lord] of all things of worship from the good of love. Signified, Explained. AC 9513. AC 9518. AC 9682.
The disposition and ordination of interior goods in exterior ones varies... according to the reception; and the reception, according to the spiritual and moral life of each one in the world.
The application of the natural man for the reception of good and truth from the Divine. Signified, Explained.
A representative of the reception of good and truth in the natural man. Signified, Explained.
Reception in the Heavens and in the Church. Signified, Explained.
The grateful hearing and reception by the Lord of all things of worship from love and charity. Signified, Explained.
(Such) cannot receive anything of the good of love and truth of faith. Signified.
Influx and illustration take place according to the faculty of reception with man; and the faculty of reception is according to the love of truth and good...
Occlusion as to the influx of good and truth, lest there be any reception. Signified, Explained.
The reception of Divine truth from the Word and thereby conjunction with the Lord. Signified, Explained.
That Divine truth and good will be revealed to those who receive. Signified, Explained.
The worship of the Lord from the truths and goods of faith and love, and thus preparation for reception. Signified, Explained.
Reception then from influx into what is external. Signified, Explained.
The enticement, reception, and appropriation of falsity from evil. Signified, Explained.
The implantation of truth in good, and its reception. Signified, Explained.
For the Lord appears to everyone according to the quality of the reception of Him...
Therefore the Heavens are distant according to the reception...
In the degree in which the Angels are receptions of Divine truth, they have light.

The Angels who receive the Divine good more, are in the Celestial Kingdom; and those who receive the Divine truth more, are in the Spiritual one. The most perfect Angels are those who receive both in a like degree.
(Such) easily receive truths (there).
When (mercy and innocence) are present, all things of faith are received as it were spontaneously.
For love... receives everything which is in agreement with itself; hence, as much as the love is, so much he receives.

The Lord from mercy leads everyone who receives Him; and he receives Him who lives according to the laws of Divine order... (Thus) he is received into Heaven who receives Heaven into himself in the world...
(Thus) the presence of the Lord is perpetual with everyone; but it is diversely received.
For all influx from the Spiritual World is varied according to the reception...
Everyone receives truth in proportion to the good in which he is.

The Lord... cannot love and dwell with man unless He is received... To enter to anyone, and remain, with whom there is no reception, is impossible. As the reception and the reciprocal in man are from the Lord, He says, Abide in Me, and I in you, etc.
That Angels and men are recipients of life. General article.
That all things... are recipients of the Divine love and Divine wisdom... General article.
Every created thing is such... as to be a recipient of God; not by continuity, but by contiguity...
As they are recipients, they are also re-agents...
The more perfect animals are recipients of the life of the three degrees of the natural world. (Continued. See Life.)
(Thus) the uses of all things are the recipients themselves of life.
Man is a recipient; and a recipient, or receptacle, is various. A wise man is a recipient of the Divine love and wisdom more adequately... than a simple one... yet the Divine is the same in each.
That the distance between the Sun and the Angels... is an appearance according to the reception of the Divine love and wisdom by them. General article.
It is on account of the differences of the reception of the Lord by the Angels that the Heavens appear distinct from each other...
Love and wisdom, that is, the Lord... cannot progress by spaces; but are with everyone according to the reception.
That... as the Angels are recipients, the Lord alone is Heaven. General article.
The habitations of Angels and Spirits are spiritual, because they dwell according to the receptions of love and wisdom from the Lord.
That the quarters (there)... are from the Angels according to the reception. General article.
Love and wisdom proceed as a one; but are not received as a one.
The Lord is the same with (all); but the recipients... are unlike, from an unlike reception and life.
The universal Heaven is in this effigy... because the Angels... are recipients of love and wisdom from the Lord; and recipients are images.
(Good) can be turned into evil by the recipient subject...
Be faithful unto death = the reception and acknowledgement of Truths...
That these things will not be received until after the dragon has been cast out of the World of Spirits; because there would be danger if they were received before. Signified, Explained.
How this doctrine would be received in the Church before (this). Signified, Explained.
Concerning the difficult reception of the doctrine of the New Church. Treated of. AR 535.
No others are received by the Lord.
Women are born loves, and men... receptions. CL 161:end. (Shown by experiment). CL 216. a. CL 379.
That wives... have a state of preparation for reception. Explained.
(This) greatly injures their state of reception, which is prepared according to the state of the husband's ability.
Love and wisdom... are inspired according to the reception; and the reception is according to the love of being wise.
In all conjunction by love there must be action, reception, and reaction... The state of wisdom of husbands is reception, and also reaction...
The Lord's mere presence is without reception; but His presence and conjunction together is with reception.
In this is the state of procreation with men; and the state of reception with women.
The Divine order is that man dispose himself for the reception of God...
To prepare one's self for the reception of God... is to live according to Divine order.

If a man approaches the Lord, and worships Him alone, he comes into the power of Knowing all Truths; and therefore every true worshipper of the Lord, as soon as he hears any Truth of faith which he had not heard before, at once sees, acknowledges, and receives it. The reason is, that the Lord is in him, and he in the Lord; consequently, the light of Truth is in him, and he in the light of Truth.
Who does not know that... the grace of reception is universal?
That the things which inflow from the Lord are received by man according to his form. Explained.
How [my] writings seem to be received by men. Explained.
There are five kinds of reception (of them). Enumerated.
How many will receive that which is being written through me. Explained.
(This interior profane Spirit) could receive truths...
When Spirits are talking together, if the discourse is not received... (the speaker's) face begins to disappear...
The Angels say that they are only recipients of the Divine proceeding; and that they are Angels in the degree in which they receive it.
To see truths is of perception; and to live according to them is of reception.

They do not know that there must be the reception (of good) by man; and that reception is not possible if one does not attend to one's thoughts and intentions and the derivative deeds, and then desist from evils... In a word, unless man receives in understanding and will... there is no reception on his part, consequently, no conjunction with the Lord...
To open the door = reception on the part of man.
Those sown in good ground, are those who hear the word, and receive it, and bear fruit ().
For the Lord wills that there be reception with man; and reception exists no otherwise than by man's doing as from himself...
To open the door = reception in the heart, or life. Explained.
This perpetual will of the Lord... is not apperceived by man, for the reason that there may be reception by man; and, through reception, appropriation...
With these, the Glorification of the Lord is reception...
The reception of Divine truth and Divine good by Angels and men. Treated of.
This reception... is possible only with those who are in truth from good. Explained.
Mourning on account of the non-reception of Divine good and Divine truth. Signified, Explained.
The... reception of the Divine truth... with some, to commence the New Church. Signified, Explained.
Divine testification concerning... the reception of its doctrine. Signified, Explained.
What comes from the Lord to man must be received by man; and it cannot be received except in this... as of himself.
As light and heat are everything in the recipient, although they do not belong to it...
That man is only a recipient... (Shown by comparisons.) DLove 2. Explained.
This appearance is for the sake of reception...
There is nothing in man except the faculty of receiving.
